summary: Two articles report Indian indices marginally higher/flat as a crude oil price spike tied to geopolitical uncertainty keeps bulls sidelined — a short-horizon commodity shock that tends to benefit energy producers and weigh on discretionary and industrial demand/margins. A third item is a single-stock note on Assured Guaranty (non‑tracked) with limited short-term market relevance.

reasons: No strong recent sector catalyst was found for Communication Services.

Geopolitical-driven crude spike raises oil prices -> first-order benefit to integrated oil producers (higher revenue/margins). Second-order effects: higher fuel and input costs accelerate inflation and trim discretionary spending and raise operating costs for industrial firms and consumer goods makers, compressing margins and pressure on equities. Geopolitical uncertainty also depresses risk appetite, muting market participation (explains flat/marginal moves in Indian benchmarks).

Rising crude keeps bullish momentum in check: energy producers benefit from higher commodity prices, while higher fuel and transport costs weigh on consumption and industrial activity in the near term. The market stalemate reflects risk-off positioning as oil-driven inflation concerns offset economic optimism.
